name: Specific microbial causation of disease
summary: Robert Koch's 1876 work tied one disease to one specific microbe by experiment, a cornerstone for the idea that particular germs cause particular illnesses.
description: Koch’s 1876 evidence tied a particular infectious disease to a specific microorganism, contributing to experimental microbial causation rather than merely associating microbes with illness.
tier_reason: Specific microbial causation supports successive diagnostic, preventive and therapeutic research programmes; it is not the whole history of germ theory.

date.label: 1876 publication
date.basis: The museum chronology explicitly records publication of the results in Beiträge zur Biologie der Pflanzen in 1876.
